T2. Forward-looking reporting short-term risks (next few weeks/months) [YES] — September rainfall outlook, crop critical growth stages, sugar crushing season starting next month, RBI policy implications
T3. Forward-looking reporting long-term risks (next quarters/years) [YES] — winter crop planting cycle, next sugar cane season, sustained inflation trajectory, rupee pressure, foreign investment deterrence

Synopsis:
India's 2026 monsoon is tracking toward its weakest season in nearly two decades, driven by El Niño. Rainfall arrived 35% below normal in June, August ran a deficit, and September is forecast below-average with above-average temperatures. Key summer crops — cotton, soybean, corn, rice, sugarcane — are under moisture stress at critical growth stages. The shortfall threatens to cascade into higher food imports (vegetable oils, pulses, sugar, cotton), domestic food price inflation, and complicates RBI monetary policy at a time when retail inflation is already at 4.45% and food inflation at 5.52%. The RBI faces a stagflationary bind: weaker agricultural growth plus rising food prices, with additional pressure from Iran-linked commodity costs, rupee vulnerability, and potential foreign investment outflows.
